channel.title: Global Governance Centre - News, Events and Publications
channel.description: News, events and publications from the Global Governance Centre at the Geneva Graduate Institute

item.title: What Is Humanitarian Aid? New Exhibition Explores the Role of Design
item.description: Through kits, photography, textiles, films, audio and interactive works, Humanitarian, by Design? examines how design shapes humanitarian aid and the experience of receiving it.

item.title: Co-regulation or Outsourcing? The United Nations and the Board of Peace in Gaza
item.description: A new topical post on The Global argues that the UN’s authorization of the Board of Peace (BoP) for Gaza raises a fundamental question: is the UN engaging in meaningful co-regulation or ineffectively outsourcing its responsibilities?

item.title: Workshop – ‘Playful Design: Making International Relations Differently?
“The Politics of Governing through Methods” workshop
New project: Holding the Line: Genocide, War, and International Responsibility
item.description: Paola Gaeta has received an SNSF grant to lead the new research project "Holding the Line: Genocide, War, and International Responsibility".

item.title: The Politics of Inevitability: AI Governance and the Global Majority's Narrowing Choice
item.description: A new blog post on The Global argues that AI governance is being framed as a predetermined choice, pushing the Global Majority to align with powerful blocs rather than shape their own future. It shows how US‑, China‑, and UN‑led models compete, narrowing agency for states with limited capacity.

item.title: New project: The International Legal Infrastructure Underpinning Food Flows and Distribution
item.description: Malavika Rao has received a SNSF Postdoc.Mobility grant to lead the new research project "The International Legal Infrastructure Underpinning Food Flows and Distribution"

item.title: Art, Archives and Multilateral Futures Workshop
item.description: Geneva, 4-5 June 2026 – The Centre for Digital Humanities and Multilateralism (CDHM) hosted a two-day workshop on Art, Archives and Multilateral Futures, gathering over 50 artists, academics, archivists, and practitioners to explore the development of a new interdisciplinary research agenda and community of practice

item.title: Non-Proliferation and Disarmament Trends in the Middle East
Professor Fuad Zarbiyev Elected to Human Rights Committee
item.description: Fuad Zarbiyev , Professor of International Law at the Geneva Graduate Institute, has been elected to the United Nations Human Rights Committee for the period of 2027-2030.

item.title: Between Idealism and Pragmatism: Students Create Fictional UNSG Candidates
item.description: In the context of “Politics of International Organizations”, a class taught by Lucile Maertens , Associate Professor in Political Science and International Relations and Co-Director of the Global Governance Centre, six groups of students created fictional candidates for the position of United Nations Secretary-General (UNSG) and elaborated a series of documents for their campaign kit.

item.title: Emotions & International Law Workshop
item.description: On 4 & 5 June 2026, the Global Governance Centre will host the "Emotions & International Law Workshop" in S11 and the Fab.

item.title: Africa and the Reform of Multilateral Institutions: The 9th Pan-African Congress and the Way Forward
item.description: Professors Dêlidji Eric Degila and Fuad Zarbiyev participated in the 9th Pan-African Congress , which took place in Lomé, Togo from 8-12 December.

item.title: James Hollway on Professing Global Governance at the Institute
item.description: James Hollway has been promoted to full professor of International Relations/Political Science. He is also Co-Director of the Global Governance Centre. In this interview, he reflects on his research and how his role has evolved since arriving at the Geneva Graduate Institute in 2015.
